q: I have black and white keys but I never open a door, and when you press me I play a tune. What am I?
note: Its black and white keys make melodies, not open doors.

q: What has two hands and a face but can never clap or smile?
note: A clock's 'hands' point to the hours and minutes.

q: What gets wetter and wetter the more it dries?
note: A towel soaks up water as it dries you off.

q: Paheli: Ek thaal moti se bhara, sabke sar par ulta dhara; chaaron or woh thaal phire, moti usse ek na gire. (A plate full of pearls, held upside down over everyone's head.)
note: The upturned plate is the sky; its pearls are the stars that never fall.

q: Paheli: Hari thi man bhari thi, laakh moti jadi thi; raja ji ke baag mein dushaala odhe khadi thi. What is it?
note: The shawl is the husk; the pearls are kernels on the cob.

q: I have one eye but cannot see, and thread must pass through me before I can work. What am I?
note: The hole at the top of a needle is called its eye.

q: I have a neck but no head, and I wear a cap to stop what's inside from spilling. What am I?
note: The narrow top part of a bottle is called its neck.

q: I'm tied to a string at birthday parties, I grow bigger when you blow into me, and I pop if squeezed too hard. What am I?
note: Most party balloons are made of latex or foil.

q: Paheli: Kaali hai par kaag nahi, lambi hai par naag nahi; bal khaati hai par dor nahi, baandhte hain par dhor nahi. (Black but not a crow, long but not a snake, twisted but not a rope.)
note: A braid of hair is black, long, twisted and tied up with ribbon.

q: Paheli: Hari dandi, laal kamaan; tauba tauba kare insaan. (A green stalk, a red bow, and it makes people cry 'tauba'.)
note: A red chilli is curved like a bow and makes eaters gasp.

q: The more of these you take, the more of them you leave behind. What are they?
note: Every step forward leaves a footprint behind you.

q: I can travel all around the world while staying stuck in one corner. What am I?
note: A postage stamp stays in the corner of a letter as it crosses countries.

q: I have cities but no houses, forests but no wood, and seas but no fish, and I fold up flat. What am I?
note: A map shows cities, forests and seas as symbols on paper.

q: Paheli: Bahar se main hara-bhara, andar se bilkul laal; kaale kaale beej chhupaaun, garmi mein karun kamaal. What am I?
note: Green rind, red flesh, black seeds: a summer favourite.

q: Paheli: Kaala ghoda, safed sawaari; ek utri, doosri ki baari. (A black horse with white riders; one gets off, then the next one's turn.) Which kitchen pair is it?
note: The black griddle carries one white roti after another.

q: What goes up and up as the calendar turns, and never, ever comes down?
note: Your age rises with every birthday and can never go back.

q: I'm tall when I'm young and small when I'm old, and wax runs down my sides as I glow. What am I?
note: A lit candle melts its own wax, so it shrinks as it burns.

q: I'm full of holes, yet I can still hold water. What am I?
note: A sponge's tiny pores trap water inside.

q: Paheli: Paani se nikla ped ek, paat nahi par daal anek; is ped ki thandi chhaaya, par neeche koi baith na paaya. What is it?
note: A fountain's jets spread like branches, but nobody can sit beneath them.

q: Paheli: Aadi kate toh geet sunaaun, madhya kate toh sant ban jaaun, ant kate toh saath nibhaaun; poora main sabke man bhaaun. Kaun sa shabd?
note: San-gee-t: drop san = geet, drop gee = sant, drop t = sangi (companion).

q: What question can you never truthfully answer with a 'yes'?
note: If you really were asleep, you couldn't answer at all.

q: It is always ahead of you, yet you can never see it. What is it?
note: The future is always ahead of you, but no one can see it.

q: What can you catch but never throw?
note: You 'catch' a cold from germs, but can't toss it away.

q: Paheli: Teen akshar ka mera naam, ulta seedha ek samaan; paani par main chalta jaaun, maal musaafir paar lagaaun. What am I?
note: Ja-haa-j reads the same both ways in Devanagari.

q: Paheli: Ek naari ke do baalak, dono ek hi rang; ek phire, ek thaada rahe, phir bhi dono sang. (Two same-coloured 'children': one spins, one stays still.)
note: In a hand chakki the top stone turns while the bottom stone stays put.

q: I have branches but no leaves, no trunk and no fruit, and you can open an account with me. What am I?
note: Bank branches are offices of the same bank in different places.

q: What can fill an entire room but takes up no space at all?
note: Light spreads through a room without occupying any space.

q: The more of me there is, the less you can see. What am I?
note: The deeper the darkness, the less you can make out.

q: Paheli: Do dhaar, do chhed, ungliyon se chalun; kapda ho ya kaagaz, beech se kaat daalun. What am I?
note: Two blades pivot on one screw, with finger holes to work them.

q: Paheli: Safed murgi, hari poonch; na maane toh kisi se poochh. (A white hen with a green tail.)
note: A white radish with its leafy green top.

q: I have a spine but no bones, and my pages are full of words, yet I never speak. What am I?
note: A book's spine is the edge that holds its pages together.

q: I run but never walk, have a mouth but never talk, and a bed but never sleep. What am I?
note: Rivers 'run', end at a mouth and flow along a riverbed.

q: What can you break without ever touching it?
note: You break a promise simply by not keeping it.

q: Paheli: Ek phool kaale rang ka, sar par sada suhaaye; tez dhoop mein khil jaaye, chhaaya mein murjhaaye. (A black flower that opens in harsh heat and folds in the shade.)
note: It opens up against the heat and folds away indoors.

q: Paheli: Kaali kaali maa, laal laal bachche; jidhar jaaye maa, udhar jaayein bachche. (A black mother whose red children follow wherever she goes.)
note: The black engine is the mother; the red coaches follow it everywhere.

q: I'm lighter than a feather, yet even the strongest person can't hold me for an hour. What am I?
note: Even record-holding freedivers can't hold their breath for an hour.

q: I pass through cities and fields and climb over hills, yet I never move at all. What am I?
note: A road stretches across places but stays perfectly still.

q: Paheli: Ek kahaani main kahoon, sunn le mere poot; bina paron ke ud gaya, baandh gale mein soot. (It flew without wings, with a thread tied at its neck.)
note: It flies with no wings, held by its string.

q: Paheli: Baala tha jab sabko bhaaya, bada hua kuch kaam na aaya; kavi ne keh diya uska naav, arth karo nahi chhodo gaanv. What is it?
note: 'Baala' means lit, 'badhaana' means to put out a lamp; the answer hides in 'keh diya'.

q: What has four legs but can't walk, and holds your plate at dinner?
note: Tables stand on four legs but never go anywhere.

q: Which kind of building is packed with thousands of stories, even if it has just one floor?
note: The pun: stories you read, not storeys as in floors.

q: What kind of room has no doors and no walls, and pops up in damp soil after rain?
note: It's a 'room' only in name: mush-room.

q: Paheli: Laal laal aankhen, lambe lambe kaan; rui ka phaaha, bolo kya hai naam? (Red eyes, long ears, soft as a cotton ball.)
note: White rabbits often have pinkish-red eyes and long ears.

q: Paheli: Ek ped mein baarah daali, har daali mein tees patte; aadhe patte kaale, aadhe patte ujle. (One tree, twelve branches, thirty leaves each, half dark and half bright.)
note: Twelve months of about thirty days, each split into night and daylight.

q: What has thirteen hearts but no other organs?
note: A standard deck has 13 cards in the hearts suit.

q: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
note: Count the letter: minute has one, moment has two, thousand years none.

q: I'm black when you buy me, red when you use me, and grey when you throw me away. What am I?
note: Charcoal glows red while burning and ends up as grey ash.

q: Paheli: Ek ghar aisa jismein na koi dwaar na raasta; andar rehta peela raja. (A house with no way in at all, and a yellow king inside.)
note: The shell has no opening; the yolk is the yellow king.

q: What begins with T, ends with T, and has T inside it?
note: Its name starts and ends with T, and the brew inside sounds like T too.

q: Which invention lets you look straight through a solid wall?
note: A window is simply a see-through opening built into a wall.

q: What is always dressed but never wears any clothes?
note: Salads get 'dressing' poured over them instead of clothes.

q: Paheli: Patti ubli doodh ke sang, adrak daalo toh badhe umang; nukkad nukkad bikti hoon, tapri pe bhi milti hoon. What am I?
note: Roadside tapris serve it piping hot from morning till night.

q: Paheli: Teen pahiye, peela-hara rang, meter chale ya mol-bhaav ka dhang; galiyon mein phurr se nikal jaaun. What am I?
note: Delhi's CNG autos are painted green and yellow.

q: I can't speak, but I answer back whenever you shout at me across a valley. What am I?
note: An echo is sound bouncing back off hills or walls.

q: I shave many times a day, yet my own beard stays exactly the same. Who am I?
note: A barber shaves customers, not his own face.

q: What can you hold in your right hand but never in your left hand?
note: Your left hand can't reach round to grip its own elbow.

q: Forward I am heavy, but spell me backward and I am not. What am I?
note: 'Ton' reversed spells 'not'.

q: What five-letter word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
note: Add 'er' to it and it literally becomes 'shorter'.

q: What starts with E, ends with E, and usually has only one letter inside?
note: An envelope holds a letter, the kind you post.

q: Paheli: Lakdi ka main, ek taraf chapta ek taraf ubhra; haath mein handle, gend ko door udaaun, chauke-chhakke lagaaun. What am I?
note: The ridged back of a cricket bat adds strength behind its flat hitting face.

q: Paheli: Kai manzil ki building, har manzil mein khaana; school-office saath chalun, dopahar mein khul jaana. What am I?
note: Stacked steel tiers keep dal, sabzi and roti separate until lunch.

q: I'm so fragile that a single word spoken aloud breaks me. What am I?
note: The moment anyone speaks, silence is gone.

q: I have a bow but tie no ribbon, four strings but no puppet, and I sit tucked under a player's chin. What am I?
note: A violin is played by drawing a bow across its strings.

q: What kind of coat can only be put on while it is wet?
note: Paint goes on wet and dries on the wall.

q: Paheli: Teen haath hain mere, sar ke upar ghoomun; garmi mein sabka saathi, switch dabao toh jhoomun. What am I?
note: Most Indian ceiling fans have three blades.

q: Paheli: Lakdi ka main lamba sa, chakle par daudta jaaun; aate ki loi ko gol gol roti banaaun. What am I?
note: It rolls dough balls flat on a round chakla.

q: I have lots of eyes but cannot see; I grow underground and end up as chips and fries. What am I?
note: The small buds on a potato's skin are called eyes.

q: What is white when it's dirty and black when it's clean?
note: Chalk dust makes it white; wiping it restores the black.

q: I am a small cube with six faces and twenty-one dots in all, and I decide your moves in board games. What am I?
note: The faces numbered 1 to 6 add up to 21 dots.

q: Paheli: Aage do seedhe-saadhe saathi seengon wale, peeche lakdi ka ghar; pahiye gaayein charr-charr, gaon ki kachchi sadak par. What am I?
note: Pairs of oxen still pull these carts along many village roads.

q: I go in dry and come out wet, and the longer I stay in, the stronger the drink gets. What am I?
note: Leave it steeping longer and the brew gets darker and stronger.

q: Which long place name has four eyes but cannot see?
note: Mississippi contains the letter i four times.

q: Which letter is always full of water, just by the way it sounds?
note: Say it aloud: the letter C sounds like 'sea'.

q: Paheli: Gol gol phooli, andar se khaali; khatta-meetha paani bharke, ek hi baar mein khaa li. What am I?
note: Each one is cracked open, filled and eaten in a single bite.

q: What kind of cup can you eat but never drink from?
note: A cupcake is a small cake baked in a paper case.

q: What do you get when you put a car and a pet together, then lay it on the floor?
note: Car plus pet spells carpet.

q: What kind of key opens a banana?
note: Monkeys famously peel bananas; the 'key' is only in the name.

q: Paheli: Chaar rang ki gotiyaan, chhakka aaye toh ghar se niklein; na saanp na seedhi, phir bhi sab ghar pahunchne ko bhaagein. Which game?
note: Each player races four tokens of one colour to the centre home.

q: Paheli: Chaar kone, chaar jebein, beech mein laal 'queen'; ungli se striker maaro, gotiyan jebon mein jaani. What am I?
note: Pocketing the red queen needs a follow-up cover shot.

q: What word still has 'some' left even after you take away the whole?
note: Remove 'whole' from this word and 'some' remains.

q: Which English word has three double letters in a row, one pair right after another?
note: b-OO-KK-EE-per: three pairs back to back.

q: I'm always hungry and must keep being fed, and any finger that touches me turns red. What am I?
note: Fire needs fuel to keep going and burns skin on contact.

q: Paheli: Raat ko gaana gaaun, kaan ke paas bhinbhinaaun; chupke se kaat ke ud jaaun, sabki neend udaaun. What am I?
note: Only female mosquitoes bite; males feed on plant nectar.

q: Paheli: Ek jaanwar aisa, jiski dum par paisa. (An animal with 'money' on its tail.)
note: Its tail's shimmering eye-spots look like rows of shiny medallions.

q: We come as a pair, rest on your nose, hook over your ears, and help you see clearly. What are we?
note: Spectacles perch on the nose and ears to correct vision.

q: I show you everything reversed, so your left becomes my right, yet I never move a muscle. What am I?
note: A mirror flips images left to right.

q: I am black and white and 'red' all over, and I land at your door each morning. What am I?
note: 'Red' sounds like 'read', and a newspaper is read everywhere.

q: Paheli: Teen akshar ka shabd hoon, beech ka akshar kate toh 'nar' reh jaaun; bahut saare log mujh mein basein, gaon se bada kehlaaun. Kaun sa shabd?
note: Na-ga-r: drop the middle 'ga' and 'nar' (man) is left.

q: I lose my head every morning and get it back again every night. What am I?
note: Your head leaves the pillow at dawn and returns at night.

q: I have a page for every date on the calendar, and you write about your day in me each night. What am I?
note: Many people keep one to record thoughts and memories.

q: What can you serve again and again, but never eat?
note: In tennis, every point starts with a serve.

q: Paheli: Samundar ke paani se bana, dhoop mein sookh ke safed hua; khaane mein na ho toh sab pheeka. What am I?
note: Salt pans along India's coasts dry out seawater into crystals.

q: Paheli: Chulhe se janma, hawa mein khoya; aankhon ko jalaake sabko rulaaya. What am I?
note: Smoke irritates the eyes and makes them water.

q: People throw me out when they want to use me, and pull me back in when they're done. What am I?
note: An anchor is dropped to hold a boat and hauled up to leave.

q: I can be cracked, made, told and played, but never touched. What am I?
note: You crack, make, tell or play a joke.

q: Which word contains all twenty-six letters but has only three syllables?
note: Al-pha-bet: three syllables holding every letter from A to Z.

q: Paheli: Kaale kaale baalak upar ghoomein, bina pankh ke udte jaayein; garjein toh dharti par paani barsaayein. What are they?
note: Dark rain clouds gather and rumble before a downpour.

q: Paheli: Jeb mein rehta, ghanti bajaata, door baithe logon se baat karaata; touch karo toh jaag jaata. What am I?
note: Touchscreen phones wake up with a tap or a swipe.

q: What begins with P, ends with E, and holds thousands of letters?
note: It starts with P, ends with E, and is full of mail.

q: Which word names both the flat inside of your hand and a tall tropical plant with large feathery leaves?
note: Hand palms and palm trees share the same English word.

q: I'm knitted into socks, scarves and sweaters, chased by playful cats in a ball, and I come from sheep. What am I?
note: Wool is sheared from sheep and spun into yarn.

q: Paheli: Kadvi meri patti, kadvi meri daatun; aangan mein chhaaya doon, phir bhi sab kahein gunon ki khaan. Which tree am I?
note: Neem twigs have long been chewed as natural toothbrushes.

q: Paheli: Do bhai saath chalein, pairon ke neeche rahein; chat-chat awaaz karein, ghar ke bahar utar jaayein. What are they?
note: Many Indian homes ask guests to leave footwear at the door.

q: What flies without wings and never lands, no matter how hard you try to catch it?
note: 'Time flies' means time passes quickly.

q: I'm always on my way but I never arrive; when you reach me, I have already become today. What am I?
note: Tomorrow turns into today the moment it comes.

q: What goes up and down all day long but never moves an inch?
note: A staircase leads up and down but stays fixed in place.

q: Paheli: Chaawal-daal ka ghol, garam lohe pe phaila gol; patla aur kurkura, saath mein chutney anmol. What am I?
note: The batter is fermented overnight, which gives it a slight tang.

q: Paheli: Seenkon ka parivaar, ek dori mein bandha; ghar ka kachra saaf karaaun, kone mein khada. What am I?
note: Seenk versions use stiff ribs; phool jhaadu uses soft grass.

q: I follow you everywhere on a bright day, copying every move, but I disappear on a pitch-black night. What am I?
note: A shadow appears wherever your body blocks a source of brightness.

q: What runs around the whole garden without ever moving?
note: A fence 'runs' along the edge of a garden but stays put.

q: I have a tongue but can't taste, and holes for laces but no eyes to see; you wear me on your feet. What am I?
note: A shoe's tongue is the flap under its laces.

q: Paheli: Lakdi ki poshaak, andar kaala dil; jitna likhoon utna chhota hota jaaun. What am I?
note: Sharpening shaves away its wooden coat to expose a fresh tip.

q: Paheli: Kaagaz par likha mitaaun, khud ghis ghis ke chhota ho jaaun; school bag ki pakki saheli. What am I?
note: The material rubber got its English name from being used to rub out marks on paper.

q: What gets sharper the more you use it?
note: Practice sharpens the mind, while blades grow dull with use.

q: Which letter is always found at the end of a rainbow?
note: The word 'rainbow' ends with the letter W.

q: A child can blow me into the air and I shimmer with colours, but I burst the moment you try to hold me. What am I?
note: A bubble's thin film shows shifting colours before it pops.

q: Paheli: Chaabi se khulun, chaabi se band; darwaaze pe latka rahun, ghar ki karun rakhwaali. What am I?
note: It guards the door without ever moving from its latch.

q: Paheli: Bahar se sakht jata-dhaari, andar safed malaai; usmein chhupa meetha paani, garmi mein sabko bhaayi. What am I?
note: A tender green one holds far more water than a mature brown one.

q: The more I'm used, the smaller I get, and I leave you cleaner after every bath. What am I?
note: A bar wears away a little with every wash.

q: I have a space you can't sit in, keys that open nothing and an Enter that isn't a door, but no screen of my own. What am I?
note: A keyboard has a space bar, dozens of keys and an Enter key.

q: I'm made of water, yet you can stand on me; leave me out on a hot day and I'll quietly run away. What am I?
note: Ice is frozen water that melts back into liquid above 0°C.

q: Paheli: Lohe ki meri gardan, haath pakad ke hilaao; dharti ke andar se thanda paani nikalwaao. What am I?
note: Villages across India use these to draw groundwater by hand.

q: Paheli: Do pahiye, ek ghanti, pedal maaro toh daudun; na petrol na diesel, bas tumhare pairon se chalun. What am I?
note: Pedal power is all it needs to move.

q: I have many teeth but never eat, and I hold your jacket shut when winter winds blow. What am I?
note: A zipper's two rows of teeth mesh together.

q: I have a handle and wheels, and I carry your clothes on every trip, yet I never wear them. What am I?
note: A suitcase carries clothes; it never wears them.

q: I have a thousand wheels but I never move; drivers leave their cars on me and walk away. What am I?
note: All those wheels belong to parked cars, not to the lot.

q: Paheli: Raat ko aaun, din mein chhup jaaun; kabhi aadha, kabhi poora, kabhi bilkul na dikh paaun. What am I?
note: On amavasya night it can't be seen at all.

q: Paheli: Subah poorab se nikloon, shaam ko pashchim mein chhip jaaun; saara din roshni baantoon, garmi bhi main laaun. What am I?
note: It rises in the east and sets in the west.

q: Which vehicle's name is spelled exactly the same forwards and backwards?
note: R-A-C-E-C-A-R reads the same either way.

q: What can you see in a still pond that never gets wet?
note: A reflection sits on the water's surface but is only an image.

q: Paheli: Ek chhota sa paudha, sabse zyaada sharmaaye; ungli se chhoo lo toh, pattiyaan band kar jaaye. Which plant?
note: Its leaflets fold up within seconds of being touched.

q: Paheli: Rang bhara pet mera, dabaao toh dhaar chhod doon; Holi ke din galiyon mein, sabko rang mein bhigo doon. What am I?
note: A squirter with a plunger that sprays coloured water.

q: Which English word still sounds exactly the same after you remove its last four letters?
note: Drop 'ueue' and the single letter Q sounds identical.

q: I have four fingers and a thumb but I'm not alive, and I keep your hand warm in winter. What am I?
note: Gloves have separate fingers; mittens don't.

q: I ring when a visitor arrives, and you answer me without saying a word. What am I?
note: In Indian English it's often called a 'calling bell'.

q: Paheli: Hara rang, laal chonch; jo sikhaao wahi dohraaun, pinjre mein reh ke bhi meethi baatein sunaaun. What am I?
note: Rose-ringed parakeets are India's common green, red-beaked parrots.

q: Paheli: Teen akshar ka shabd hoon, ulta seedha ek samaan; chehre par do do milte, dekhne ka karte kaam. Kaun sa shabd?
note: Na-ya-n reads the same both ways and means eyes.

q: If you have me, you want to share me; once you share me, you no longer have me. What am I?
note: Once a secret is told, it isn't a secret anymore.

q: I'm an odd number, but take away one letter and I become even. Which number am I?
note: Drop the S from 'seven' and 'even' is left.

q: Which bird can lift the heaviest loads on a building site?
note: Cranes are tall wading birds and also heavy-lifting machines.

q: Paheli: Teen akshar ka shabd, pehla kate toh sunne ka kaam; beech kate toh soche jo, poora raho toh rehne ka dhaam. Kaun sa shabd?
note: Ma-kaa-n: drop ma = kaan (ear), drop kaa = man (mind).
